blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A record implements `Serializable`, and its compact constructor refuses a negative age. A byte stream saved with age -1 is read back. What happens?

options.text: Reading it fails, because the stream's values go through the same validation again
options.says: The page says a record is deserialized through its canonical constructor, so the constructor's validation also runs.

options.text: Reading it succeeds, because the stream's values are copied straight into the fields
options.says: That is how an ordinary class is read back; the page says a record goes through its canonical constructor instead.

options.text: Reading it succeeds, because the record's own checks run only when `new` is called
options.says: The page says the constructor's validation also runs on deserialization, not only for new.

concepts: A Serializable record is deserialized through its canonical constructor, so its validation runs again.
